_comment: Developer field run: tools/dev/collect-macos-field-report.sh asks a developer ErgoptiPlus.app (infra/dev_source.lua) to run every Debug field check, the diagnostics collection and the AI download flows, then copies the results it wrote. Read at run time by infra/field_run.lua, which starts only in developer source mode, and by the collector through plutil. The folder is relative to the clone root; a step's deadline is in seconds and never exceeds what is left of the request's own deadline. An AI step with progress_max_seconds is a download: its deadline is the longest it may stay without progress, each window with progress grants another, and progress_max_seconds bounds it; the default request deadline covers every step at its bound, and the collector waits that long plus its own grace. A step that needs a person is reported with that verdict and its reason, never run with a stand-in. Each step's proves line says in one sentence what its pass shows; docs/memory/macos-hammerspoon.md (project-macos-field-run-step-details) keeps each step's codes and reading notes.

guided._comment: A guided step (infra/field_run_guided.lua) writes the prompt file in the folder with the exact gesture; the collector prints it, and for an attest step (or to skip) writes the answer file {step, answer} with pass, fail or skip. An observe step reads its check before the prompt and every poll_seconds until each until step rose (or turned to a failure); no gesture within gesture_seconds is needs_person.

steps.proves: A Mac without Ergopti's own Karabiner runtime gets it installed with no click of Ergopti's (the macOS administrator prompt is the one human step), and pqrs' driver is reported active once macOS approved it.
The driver reloads after the install, so the owner admits the installed runtime before the owned checks run.

The Karabiner lease is healthy: CLI present, lease phase, guardian ready, no lease failure, key loss or swallowed key this session; the lease answers that timed out, the free memory and the last karabiner.json write (size, time) are named.
The Ergopti-owned Karabiner runtime is still dormant, what of it and of the stock Karabiner is installed or running, and whether the owner would accept the installed VirtualHIDDevice.
While Ergopti runs, its pinned Karabiner runtime is downloaded and verified, ready, and holds the user's Karabiner closed with the close recorded (after a resume too).
The managed download chain works: system proxy kinds, PAC download, route lookup, TLS trust, one HEAD transfer and one download of the pinned input whose SHA-256 and size match its pin.
The timer service, the Shortcuts tool, Homebrew and the Karabiner-Elements signature and Gatekeeper verdict behave as assumed.
What starts Ergopti or Hammerspoon at login, whether each entry belongs to this copy, and what an ad hoc build did to its stale remap guardian registrations before registering.
The layout composer installs, enables and removes its check layout through the real path.
The boot that started the app completed, with its wall and CPU totals and its slowest stage named.
Over a quiet window the driver's own CPU share stays under the declared bound, and its memory, heap and main-thread holds are named.

With no logout, a new layout build typing the symbols first is selected and read back, a second build replaces it live and retires it, and the user's selected and enabled input sources are put back exactly.
Accessibility is granted, the other privacy grants are named, and the running bundle's identifier and strict signature are the declared ones.
Every keymap event tap is enabled, the tap watchdog runs, and the run loop answers a timer within 250 ms; holds, the worst hold with its file and line, late keys and the Lua heap are named.
The selected and enabled input sources are readable, and every installed Ergopti .keylayout and bundle Info.plist parses.

The keystats database passes SQLite's read-only quick check (and the deferred keystats start's main-thread hold is named), every configuration file parses, the logs folder takes a write and the file watchers are owned.
The launcher resolves, its headless HTTP worker role refuses malformed arguments with EX_USAGE, and it carries one direct GET to a loopback server the check owns.
Every external host the drivers declare (GitHub and its API, Hugging Face, Ollama and its registry) answers one HEAD through the managed transport.
The host the Ollama registry redirects a model blob to is one the route inventory plans, so the daemon's pull behind a PAC takes the planned route.
Without a person: the app types a fixed sequence into its own scratch field only, the tap sees each key once, the field holds it exactly and the previous app gets the focus back.

Ctrl+Caps Lock: the secondary_capslock slot is bound when assigned, and a physical Ctrl+Caps Lock pressed during this session reached it: a chord seen and never delivered fails never_delivered, no chord seen is a skip.
Every touch frame of this session carried the trackpad's capture stamp, which gesture timing uses, and the stamps are about 8 ms apart; no touch this session is a skip.
Without a person: a shipped hotstring typed with its terminator into the app's own scratch field, through the real keymap path, leaves exactly its expansion there.
Without a person: with an installed model, a short neutral text typed into the app's own scratch field brings up the prediction tooltip, and how long it took is named.
One rebuild of the menu tree succeeds; its duration, its top-level rows and the slowest ones are named.
The Debug menu's bug-report snapshot collects completely; its codes count its warnings and errors.
The Ollama runtime installs or is reused through the AI menu's install path.
The Ollama server starts, pulls the smallest catalogue model (an installed one first) and lists it.
The MLX environment bootstraps or is reused through the backend selection path.
The MLX model download and serve path works with the smallest installed catalogue model, and the active-model file is put back.
Each AI download whose PAC or WPAD could not be used named a pac_unavailable_fallback stage, then logged that the direct connection worked; a working PAC reports no_pac_failure.
The owned Ollama passes a strict signature check, its running server lists its models and predicts one token with an installed model; the MLX models on disk are counted.
The Metrics tables events_window_topo, events_av and events_network are readable and their row count per declared kind is named; the guided steps compare it before and after a gesture.

Today's log names the busiest slow segment and hold phase, the worst ingest, save, window probe and diagnostics stage with its forks, and no failed lease start, layout misread, keystats lock or unregistered shortcut.

Today's log has no touch frame without its capture stamp, window-toggle error or rolled-back hotstring start, and counts gate-rejected three-finger candidates, text moved off a held key and activity-cancelled predictions.
A FIFO is classified as a named pipe without being opened, and neither the append nor the atomic write of the file system adapter opens or replaces it.
Every local AI server of local_servers.json has a discovery descriptor the driver accepts, and one read-only sweep names where each was looked for and what answered.
No crash report of the last day for the app's processes; other apps' reports, CPU and memory are named, with where it goes: footprint and peak, largest resident regions and the Lua heap.
Every managed tap manipulator of the deployed Karabiner configuration carries the delay the shared tap-hold model asks for: the key's own delay when it has one, the global delay otherwise (PAR-15).

The copy a tap-hold key sends reaches the pasteboard: the lone tap window Karabiner got, a readable counter, and how many copies since start were verified, retried or lost, without typing or writing the clipboard.

The run_apple_shortcut action lists the Shortcuts library through its owner and command-line transport, and runs the shortcut named Ergopti Field Test end to end when the library holds one (skipped by name otherwise).

steps.gesture: Metrics on: move a window, resize it, make it full screen and back, then drag it to a second screen (a Mac with one screen: press s to skip).
steps.proves: Each window gesture adds its events_window_topo row (move, resize, state change, monitor change) within the ingest period.

steps.gesture: Open Zoom or OBS (or start a QuickTime screen recording), wait 40 s, then quit it (press s if none is installed).
steps.proves: A screen-capture or conferencing application adds its events_av screen_recording_start row.

steps.gesture: Turn Wi-Fi off, wait 40 s, turn it back on and wait 40 s (Ethernet: unplug and plug it back). Connect no VPN during this step.
steps.proves: Internet loss and return add events_network internet_down and internet_up rows, and a tunnel left idle (iCloud Private Relay) adds no vpn_connected row.

steps.gesture: Connect a VPN (WireGuard or the system IPsec client), wait 30 s, disconnect it and wait 30 s (press s if no VPN is configured).
steps.proves: A VPN connection and disconnection add events_network vpn_connected and vpn_disconnected rows.

steps.gesture: Press Ctrl+Caps Lock once, in any app.
steps.proves: A physical Ctrl+Caps Lock reaches the secondary_capslock slot: seen and delivered passes, seen and never delivered fails never_delivered.

steps.gesture: In TextEdit, type asa then Space fast twenty times, also holding the a of the trigger down; then undo it.
steps.proves: The hotstring carrier moved its text off the held trigger key (Synthetic text moved off a held key), counted in the day log.

steps.gesture: In Safari with several tabs, scroll with two fingers for a while, then do deliberate vertical three-finger swipes: slow, flick, staggered, after a scroll, finger resting, ten half a second apart.
steps.proves: Every touch frame of the swipes carried the trackpad's capture stamp (no unstamped frame); whether each swipe switched exactly one tab is the next attested step.

steps.gesture: With the AI on and a model installed, type a few words in TextEdit until a prediction shows, then move the pointer; repeat with a scroll and a click elsewhere.
steps.proves: User activity cancels a pending prediction, one User activity line per cancellation at DEBUG.

steps.gesture: Did each deliberate three-finger swipe of the previous step switch exactly one tab, and minutes of two-finger scrolls switch none?
steps.proves: The person saw the swipes switch exactly one tab each and the scrolls none.

steps.gesture: With Caps Lock set to Enter on tap and Ctrl on hold: brush Caps Lock very briefly (about 20 ms) in TextEdit: nothing is typed and no Ctrl stays held; a normal 60 ms tap types Enter; Space still types at once in fast typing. Pass if all three hold.
steps.proves: Karabiner's owned minimum tap (to_delayed_action, apply_tap_minimum) drops a bounce, keeps a real tap and delays no ordinary key; the keyboard is read below the event system, so only the person sees it.

steps.gesture: Options « Un tap ou un hold sur une touche tap-hold commence un nouveau mot » on and « Un raccourci clavier commence un nouveau mot » off: a tap-hold copy (Cmd+C tap) between two words makes the next word-start hotstring fire, your own Cmd+C does not, no F20 reaches TextEdit or a Finder rename; switched off the option keeps the word; Caps Lock held as Ctrl/Cmd follows the same options; Ctrl held before the key still gives Ctrl+Enter; no context-menu key reaches TextEdit or a Finder rename.
steps.proves: The tap-hold word reset follows both options through Karabiner's tagged F20 and untagged application key, with no stray key in the focused app.

steps.gesture: After the onboarding number-row order was applied and the reload done, type the whole number row in TextEdit, unshifted then shifted: the symbols are the ones the onboarding offered.
steps.proves: The number row typed after the reload matches the order the onboarding applied.

steps.gesture: With French (or ABC) as the input source, choose Keyboard layout > Layout to emulate > Ergopti➕ and type in TextEdit: letters, Shift, Caps Lock, Option levels and ^ then e gives ê; Cmd+Z undoes where Ergopti has z; a row switched off types French; a hotstring fires on emulated text; the French dead ^ types its emulated character; an Option chord works in Terminal; a password field types the system layout (Secure Event Input).
steps.proves: Layout emulation types Ergopti➕ over a system layout, keeps shortcuts and hotstrings, and stops at Secure Event Input as documented.

steps.gesture: Type three ordinary hotstrings in Edge, VS Code and a terminal each: each expands once, with the right case and no stray character.
steps.proves: Ordinary hotstrings expand in Edge, VS Code and a terminal.

steps.gesture: Right after the reload, with the AI off, press the shortcut bound to open_model_browser (it opens); cover it with another window and press it again (it is raised); minimise it and press it once more (it is restored).
steps.proves: A window-toggle action opens its page right after a reload with the AI off and raises a covered or minimised one, with no window_toggle error.

steps.gesture: In the menu: Clear and Restore per category and global; Shortcuts group restore and clear; the tap delay row and « Use global delay (…) »; the tap and hold pickers; « Combinaisons de touches »; the row order unchanged (PAR-76 R18); « Retirer les anciennes règles » on an upgrade (43); Login Items shows one Ergopti (24). The configuration guard puts your settings back after the run.
steps.proves: The menu rows behave as specified and the configuration is put back by the guard.

steps.gesture: Type: chained expansions, the magic key on ISO and ANSI, undo by Backspace, a password field, an ignored app, no wrong erase count (PAR-76 R26); tap-hold rolls; Right Option + Return/Delete/Backspace/Escape; Backspace at a word start (Terminal, TextEdit, Safari Cmd+L); CapsWord cancelled by the pointer (44).
steps.proves: The typing behaviours listed in TODO hold under the person's own keyboard.

steps.gesture: With a real local model: request floor, an explicit shortcut never held, variants, replace in flight, debounce « never », live mode; AI off disarms the keys and agent actions (PAR-65); the tooltip near the screen edges on two displays (111); with « Inline auto-type » on, the prediction is typed into a real editor.
steps.proves: The AI behaviours with a real model hold, the AI switch disarms everything, and the tooltip stays on screen.

steps.gesture: With the AI on, type until a prediction is pending, then press Cmd+Tab to another app; again, then click in another app's window; again, then press F5.
steps.proves: An application or window switch cancels a pending prediction, one User activity line per cancellation at DEBUG.

steps.gesture: Debug > Test network (here; repeat on the other network in a later run), an http:// company PAC if available (issue 101); the release notes pane in light and dark (PAR-52); a Sparkle update; a Homebrew live upgrade; MLX behind a proxy (119/130/136, code 74). Pass if what this network allows works.
steps.proves: The network and update paths available on this network work.

steps.gesture: Open each page in light and dark (PAR-81), the onboarding wizard (7), App Cloner errors, trackpad gestures (126), Diagnostics focus (122), a shared export (123); click reload menu rows while busy (held and replayed); quit while busy: both processes end within 10 s (Ergopti restarts at the next run).
steps.proves: The pages render in both themes, held menu clicks replay and a quit while busy ends both processes.

steps.gesture: With Ollama.app and a PAC proxy, enable the AI: the model downloads; hold the menu open: no lease timeout; decline a download: no error window opens.
steps.proves: Issues 100 and 99 stay fixed; the lease report names memory pressure and the second Hammerspoon's login item.

steps.gesture: Native one-shot Shift: tap Shift then a letter, a dead key and in an IME (Japanese or Chinese): one capital each; CapsWord: its key and the control payloads end it as specified.
steps.proves: One-shot Shift and CapsWord payloads behave natively under the person's keyboard.

steps.gesture: With a build/macos copy registered beside the /Applications prerelease: the Accessibility dialog names …/build/macos/ErgoptiPlus.app with no tccutil reset; trash that copy, switch the entry on: the boot resumes once.
steps.proves: Two copies share one Accessibility switch and the boot resumes once the stray copy is trashed.

steps.gesture: Installed app: VS Code bridge retirement (127), the 120 provider menu, issue 94 (tap-hold refusal, symbol-wrap clipboard).
steps.proves: The installed-app checks of TODO hold on this architecture.
The field run's own pause stops Ergopti's Karabiner runtime and gives the user's Karabiner back, and the resume is queued for after the run.
The driver reloads on request and the field run resumes at its next step; the reload's duration, request to a ready field run, is named.
